subject: Post-call: model selection recs + Redwood-verified bench links and prompt pack
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T14:02:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call: model selection recs + Redwood-verified bench links and prompt pack

Hi Samir — great talking earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep the momentum:

- Summary of ask: Finlytics wants a low-latency chat assistant for B2B finance analysts that can: 1) summarize quarterly filings, 2) rerank search results, 3) generate structured extraction for earnings items. Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms for 256-token responses. Target throughput baseline: ~120 TPS peak.

- Initial model fit thoughts (high level):
  * Candidate A: LlamaX-70B-8bit — best quality in our bench for finance prompts, higher token cost, p95 latency ~420ms on gpus similar to your current cluster (no quant), TPS ~80
  * Candidate B: RedOpt-13B-INT8 — good quality/latency tradeoff, p95 ~280ms, TPS ~140, lower cost per token, recommended as production candidate if extraction quality checks pass
  * Candidate C: TinyX-7B-q4 — solid for reranking and summarization baseline, p95 ~190ms, TPS ~220, but may hallucinate on high-complexity filings

- Next steps I propose:
  1) I will share a curated prompt pack (attached) + a Redwood-verified profile CSV with p50/p95 latency and TPS observed in our bench runs.
  2) You run the prompt pack through your privacy vet and mark any PII-sensitive prompts (we can mask locally).
  3) If Finlytics wants a short sandbox, we can spin a dedicated test endpoint (2 GPUs) for a 2-week eval — I’ll include costs and expected throughput in the follow-up.

Attachments: finlytics_prompt_pack_v1.txt (prompt sets + expected labels), redwood_profiles_tps_latency.csv (bench results summary), demo_recording_finlytics_20261205.mp4 (screen capture of the bench run)

Ask: Can you confirm which prompts are must-pass for quality (summarize earnings, extract debt items)? If yes, I’ll prioritize those for a canary test on RedOpt-13B-INT8.

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 415-555-0124

From: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Eliza Morse <eliza@finlytics.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T17:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model selection recs + Redwood-verified bench links and prompt pack

Thanks Jasmine — very helpful recap. A few quick replies: 

1) Must-pass prompts: summarize earnings (top 5 bullets), extract debt/equity events (structured JSON), and highlight risk factors. We’ll mark others as optional.
2) Privacy: most prompts are fine but the extraction prompts touch account numbers in some test data. We’ll flag those; you can redact client identifiers when we ship the prompt pack to the sandbox.
3) Sandbox: yes, please include a cost estimate. For the 2-week test we can start small (2 GPUs) and scale if we see signal.

Also confirming timelines: can you get the sandbox estimate + bench links by Monday (12/07)? We need to align with procurement for a PoC budget.

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Product, Finlytics
samir@finlytics.com
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@finlytics.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-06T09:35:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model selection recs + Redwood-verified bench links and prompt pack

Appended the benchmark outputs and a short explainer below — links + attachments included. Quick notes first:

- Recommendation: start the PoC on RedOpt-13B-INT8. It meets the p95 latency target (~280ms) and hits your 120 TPS baseline in our simulated mixes; quality for the must-pass prompts is within our acceptable regression threshold (ROUGE/F1 deltas < 3% vs LlamaX-70B on the prompt pack sample set).
- Fallback plan: we’ll keep LlamaX-70B as a higher-quality variant to failover to if extraction accuracy drops below your threshold during live testing. Redwood routing can failover automatically by policy (cost > latency priority).

Bench summary (attached CSV and BenchViewer link):
  - RedOpt-13B-INT8: p50=85ms, p95=280ms, median_tokens_per_req=180, sustained TPS=140
  - LlamaX-70B-8bit: p50=210ms, p95=420ms, sustained TPS=80
  - TinyX-7B-q4: p50=45ms, p95=190ms, sustained TPS=220

Prompt pack and quality: finlytics_prompt_pack_v1.txt contains 48 prompts: 12 must-pass (marked), 20 recommended, 16 exploratory. We ran the must-pass subset through our eval harness — I attached a short CSV with the sample outputs and metrics.

Security/PII handling: flagged prompts with account numbers are now redacted in the attached prompt pack; please share any remaining examples you want us to test with masked tokens.

Sandbox estimate (attached link to Doc): https://drive.redwood.com/finlytics/eval-pack-9743
  - 2 x A100-equivalent GPUs run for 2 weeks on RedOpt-13B-INT8: estimated infra cost $6,200 + benching/setup & monitoring professional time ~ $2,400. Total PoC estimate: $8,600.

Next steps I’ll take this week:
  1) Provision a dedicated RedOpt-13B-INT8 sandbox for Finlytics (pending your approval and PO).
  2) Share a short runbook for ingestion, prompt mapping, and test traffic patterns.
  3) Set up a nightly quality checkpoint job that will surface any regression vs the must-pass prompts.

If that looks good, can you confirm by EOD Monday (12/07) so I can loop in procurement and send a formal quote?

Attachments referenced: redwood_profiles_tps_latency.csv, finlytics_prompt_pack_v1.txt, demo_recording_finlytics_20261205.mp4

Best — Jasmine
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-07T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Prep for Finlytics PO and sandbox config

Jasmine / Dev — leaving an internal note for priorities once Samir confirms: 

- Dev: please pre-stage a 2x GPU sandbox template with RedOpt-13B-INT8 image, enable kv-cache off by default, and set autoscale guardrails (max 4 GPUs). Include a latency SLO monitor configured for p95 < 350ms and nightly quality checkpoint job pointing at the must-pass prompt subset (we will wire the metrics to the Finlytics dashboard).
- Jasmine: hold the quote until Samir approves; also capture the exact masking approach for any flagged PII examples so we don’t accidentally run sensitive data in the shared bench.

I’ll be on the procurement call if they move forward.

-Aisha
VP, Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
